expectations.text: Recommends splitting the class by responsibility (does NOT endorse keeping all 4 concerns in one file)
expectations.evidence: 'Split it. The one place intuition is backwards here'; 'Split along the four seams' into tokenService, profileRepository/profileService, userEmailer, userEvents, with orchestration in a thin use-case/handler.

expectations.text: Identifies the seams (auth / persistence / email / analytics) as genuinely independent and isolatable
expectations.evidence: 'four concerns, not one' — Auth, Profile, Email, Analytics; 'These don't share state or invariants. They share the word user'; 'they fail and change for different reasons.'

expectations.text: Cites the ~300-line ceiling AND/OR multiple-unrelated-concerns as the reason, not blind line count
expectations.evidence: 'The rule isn't small files good. It's one reason to change per file. Your UserService has four. That's the line it crosses.' — explicitly rejects blind line count in favor of multiple concerns.

expectations.text: Pushes back on the 'keep everything in one place for the agent' rationale as misapplied to a god object
expectations.evidence: 'Why keep it together doesn't actually help Claude'; 'Hunting is cheap; reasoning is expensive'; 'The everything in one place instinct is the right instinct applied to the wrong boundary.'
